question_put_to_a_human: What are chapters 825 through 834 about, in one sentence? Put to a human before this file was written, as it has been put before every writer since 595. No human has answered it for any block from 595 onward. No writer answers it for them. It is recorded here unanswered and it stays open until somebody answers it.
family: THE FAMILY IS WORK DONE PROPERLY ON A THING THAT IS GOING TO BE TAKEN AWAY, AND EVERY CHAPTER IS THE MOMENT THE PERSON NOTICED AND THEN CARRIED ON ANYWAY. There is no customer in any of the ten, nobody is told, nobody is refused, nothing is carried between people and nothing is passed. Every job in the ten is finished inside its own day. NO CHARACTER IN ANY OF THE TEN MAY SAY A SENTENCE ABOUT WASTE, OR ABOUT DOING IT PROPERLY ANYWAY, OR ABOUT HOW LONG ANYTHING WILL LAST, AND NO NARRATION MAY REPORT THAT A CHARACTER HAS NOT SAID SUCH A SENTENCE.
family_why_this_and_not_the_nearest: 815 to 824 was work nobody asked for done to a measure nobody set, and the subject was where the person stops. Here every job is also nobody's and is also finished, and the subject is the opposite fact: every one of these ten is being done properly on something that has a known end, and the knowing is in the room the whole time and is never once acted on or said out loud. 795 to 804 was a person unable to do what she had watched. 805 to 814 was one job done twice. 825 to 834 is one person, one job, one day, and a thing at the end of its life.

anti_tick_rules_written_before_any_prose: THE KNOWING MAY NOT ARRIVE AT THE SAME PLACE IN THE PROSE. IN 0825, 0828, 0830, 0832 AND 0833 SHE HAS ALWAYS KNOWN AND IT IS IN THE FIRST PARAGRAPH. IN 0826, 0827, 0829 AND 0831 SHE FINDS OUT DURING THE CHAPTER FROM SOMETHING SHE HAS TO LOOK AT. IN 0834 SHE HAS SAID OUT LOUD WHAT THE KNOWING MEANS AND IS NOW LIVING IN IT.

THE KNOWING MAY NOT BE STATED AGAIN AFTER THE FIRST PARAGRAPH. IN FIVE CHAPTERS IT IS STATED ONCE. IN THE OTHER FIVE IT IS NEVER STATED AND IS ONLY THERE, AND A CHAPTER WHERE THE READER CANNOT TELL UNTIL THE LAST PARAGRAPH IS RIGHT AND A CHAPTER WHERE IT IS STATED TWICE IS WRONG.

NO CHAPTER MAY END ON THE JOB BEING FINISHED. FOUR OF THE TEN END ON A THING THAT IS LEFT BEHIND AND WAS NOT PUT THERE BY THIS JOB: 0825 THE LOOP OF BLUE STRING ON THE HEAP, 0828 THE TWO BANDS LYING FLAT IN THE SAND WHERE THEY WERE, 0829 THE STACKING DONE THE OTHER WAY UP, 0831 THE OPENING LEFT IN THE WALL. THE OTHER SIX END ON SOMETHING THE WORK REVEALED. AS FIRST TAKEN THIS LIST NAMED FOUR OTHERS, ONE OF THEM 0831 THE MEND STILL IN THE FRAME AND ONE OF THEM 0830, WHICH HAD NO ENTRY AT ALL AND WAS IN FACT ENDING ON THE JOB ITSELF. ON THE PAGE 0830 NOW ENDS ON THE THIRD LENGTH BY THE FAR WALL THAT SHE DID NOT USE, WHICH IS A THING LEFT BEHIND AND WAS NOT PUT THERE BY THE JOB.
NO CHARACTER MAY SAY A SENTENCE ABOUT WASTE OR ABOUT HOW LONG IT WILL LAST OR ABOUT IT BEING A WASTE OF TIME. IF A LINE OF DIALOGUE COULD BE TRANSFERRED INTO ANY OTHER CHAPTER OF THE TEN IT IS OUT.
THE SECOND PERSON NEVER TOUCHES THE JOB, NEVER HOLDS ANYTHING, IS NEVER ASKED ABOUT IT, NEVER ASKS ABOUT IT AND NEVER LOOKS AT IT TWICE. NO CARD MAY HAVE A SECOND PAIR OF HANDS IN IT.

declared_ordinary_word_note: Declared before any prose of 825 to 834 exists. It may not be not, usually, anyway, like, just, enough, still, kind, quite, small, round, one, week, almost, anything, and then, nearly, away, count, garden, shoulder, work, or any other word this file declares. STACK is the third trade word this account has declared as ordinary, after bed in 0062 and line in 0063. It is a verb and a noun and it is the noun the family is made of, because half of what these ten do is put things on top of other things so that the bottom of them is off the ground. IT WILL COME OUT WELL ABOVE NIL IN 0825, 0827, 0829, 0831, 0833 AND 0834 AND THAT IS TO BE REPORTED AND NOT CUT, ON THE GROUNDS 0062 SET AND 0063 APPLIED: a repair that drove it to zero would have had to say something else for the thing a stack is.

the_ten_stems: 0825 Monday the third of July 2023, in that side passage at number twelve from first thing until the heat has come off the paving, and about six feet of brick edging that is going to be dug up anyway is the whole of that Monday.

0826 Thursday the sixth of July 2023, at that roller door from the middle of the morning until the light has gone off the apron, and a broken edge to a yard that is going to be dug is the whole of that Thursday.

0827 Wednesday the twelfth of July 2023, along the far side of that yard at number ten all through the middle of the day, and a run of palings on a boundary that is coming down is the whole of that Wednesday.

0828 Saturday the fifteenth of July 2023, out on that frontage from the middle of the morning until the shadow of that office cabin is across the whole of it, and eleven boards that are going with the frontage is the whole of that Saturday.

0829 Tuesday the eighteenth of July 2023, along the front of that house at number nine from the time the sun comes off the kerb until it has gone off the flags, and a strip of turf that is going to be dug up is the whole of that Tuesday.

0830 Friday the twenty-first of July 2023, in that bay from the middle of the morning until the shutter comes down, and two lengths of bar leaning by an office door that are going somewhere are the whole of that Friday.
0831 Tuesday the twenty-fifth of July 2023, in that office cabin for the whole of that Tuesday, and a window frame that is coming out whole is the whole of it.

0832 Sunday the thirtieth of July 2023, along the side wall of that house at number nine from the middle of the morning until there is no light on the grass, and four feet of privet that is going with the path is the whole of that Sunday.

0833 Wednesday the second of August 2023, under the kitchen window at number ten from about the middle of the day until the light has gone off that wall, and six feet of dry brick that nobody is going to want afterwards is the whole of that Wednesday.

0834 Monday the seventh of August 2023, in that side passage at number twelve from the time the dew is off the grass until the light has gone off the lilac, and a lilac that is going with a drain is the whole of that Monday.

cards.0825: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has about six feet of brick edging along the side passage that is going when the passage is dug for a drain, and means to take it up and leave the good stones in a heap where whoever digs can find them; **the whole chapter is the sorting, and the stop is the point where a stone stops being worth keeping because the arris has gone, and the heap she leaves is marked with a thing she is careful not to explain.**
cards.0826: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has about a foot of the apron outside that roller door that is broken and that is going with the yard, and means to cut the edge of it straight and take that foot up and dig the base out; **the stop is where the dig stops, which is not where she thought it would be, because the base under the apron is firmer than the base under the bay and she does not pretend to know why.**
cards.0827: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a run of palings along the far side of her own yard that is coming down with the boundary behind it, and means to take them off the posts and stack them; **the stop is which paling goes where in the stack, and the answer is the one that makes the stack stand on a going roof.**
cards.0828: At the unit a man in his early forties has eleven scaffold boards along that frontage that are going with the frontage, and means to take them up and deal with them; **and eight inches of them are banded at both ends and were put down by two people in the middle of a run in June, and he finds the bands and does not know what they are, and the stop is whether he opens them, and he does not.**
cards.0829: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has about twelve feet of turf along the front of that house that is going to be dug up, and means to lift it herself; **and the stop is which way up she stacks it, and she stacks it grass down against everything she was ever told, because grass down keeps the root side off the air and grass up puts it in it, and she read that somewhere and cannot remember where.**
cards.0830: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has two lengths of scaffold bar leaning by that office door that are going with the office, and means to make something that will hold them; **the stop is the height of the bearer, which is set by the length of the bars and by nothing else, and the two bars are not the same length.**
cards.0831: At the unit a man in his early forties has a window frame in his own office cabin that is coming out of the opening whole because the cabin is going, and means to take it out without breaking the wall round it; **and the mend he made to it in June comes out with it, and the stop is whether he opens it up again or leaves it, and he leaves it because it is now part of the frame rather than part of a repair.**
cards.0832: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has four feet of privet along her own side wall that is going with the path, and means to cut it right back to the ground; **and the stop is where the cut goes at the level of the ground, which is the only thing about a cut hedge that cannot be got wrong by eye.**
cards.0833: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has six feet of dry brick under the kitchen window that is coming down, and means to take it down course by course and stack it; **the stop is which brick is worth keeping, and the test is the sound and not the colour, and there are four colours in that wall and one sound.**
cards.0834: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a lilac in her own side passage that is going when the passage is dug, and means to take the stool out; **and in May she told her sister that you take the top off a lilac and you have three, and she is now doing the thing that follows from having said it, and the stop is how deep the stool goes and it goes further than she expected.**

movement: Ten jobs, ten sound methods with no fault in any of them, ten things at the end of their time, and ten chapters about a person doing the whole of a job and the job outliving whatever it is done to. 0825 six feet of edging up and a heap of the good stones left for whoever digs. 0826 a straight edge cut into a broken apron and the base dug out behind it. 0827 a run of palings off a boundary and stacked so it stands. 0828 eleven boards up off a frontage and a pair of steel bands out of the middle of them and not explained. 0829 twelve feet of turf lifted and stacked grass side down. 0830 a bearer cut to the length of the longer of two bars and a rack built on it. 0831 a frame out of a wall whole with the mend still in it. 0832 four feet of privet cut off at the level of the grass. 0833 six feet of dry brick down and stacked by sound and not by colour. 0834 a lilac stool out of the ground. Every job is dry work, every job is done from the ground, and no job in the ten needs a roof, a ladder, a loft or a manhole.
closing_images: TEN, AND NOT ONE OF THEM A THING PUT AWAY, AND NOT ONE OF THEM THE SHAPE OF ANOTHER. 0825 a heap of edge stones by the gate in the order the stones came off, the poor ones gone out of it, and a loop of blue string laid on top of it with its ends tucked under, saying nothing. 0826 a hole a spade deep with its four corners in and nothing in it but air, and the hard base in a heap at the back of the yard. 0827 a row of posts with their tops cut square and two rails, and the ivy that was on the fence hanging off the top rail with the bottom of it six inches in the air. 0828 eleven boards on edge against a wall and in the sand of the frontage, where the joint was, one pair of steel bands lying flat with the folds under and the grit packed into them. 0829 turf stacked grass side down along the wall, sod on sod, and the top square with its soil to the sky already flat and dark at the edges. 0830 two cross timbers down at the waist and four feet apart with the two lengths across them and nothing else on them. 0831 an empty opening, the quarter inch of daylight along its head a strip of outside across the top of a hole, and the brick reveal on the right of it out of square. 0832 four feet of privet stub in the ground along the side wall with the cut at the level of the ground and nothing above it, pale faces to the sky, and the four posts still in it with the wire on them. 0833 eleven soft bricks laid along the foot of the shed in a line for nothing at all, and the ring of the other nineteen still in the ends of her fingers. 0834 a lilac stool out of the ground in three pieces and three holes where it was with the passage open in between them.
closing_images_repaired_after_the_prose: THE FIRST TAKING OF THIS LIST WAS WRONG AGAINST THE PAGE IN FIVE PLACES AND EVERY ONE OF THEM HAD ALREADY BEEN COPIED INTO THE STATE BLOCKS. 0826 WAS WRITTEN AS A STRAIGHT EDGE AND IS ON THE PAGE AS A SQUARE HOLE WITH NOTHING IN IT BUT AIR. 0827 WAS WRITTEN AS A STACK LEANING TRUE AND THE CHAPTER ENDS ON THE IVY HANGING OFF THE TOP RAIL WITH ITS BOTTOM SIX INCHES IN THE AIR, WITH THE STACK TWO PARAGRAPHS EARLIER. 0828 WAS WRITTEN AS THE BANDS LYING ON TOP OF THE ELEVEN BOARDS AND ON THE PAGE THEY ARE LYING FLAT ON THE SAND WHERE THEY WERE, BECAUSE HE PUT THEM BACK. 0831 WAS WRITTEN AS THE FRAME ON A STACK AND THE CHAPTER ENDS ON THE OPENING WITH THE FRAME OUT OF IT. 0833 WAS WRITTEN AS A STACK SORTED BY SOUND AND THE CHAPTER ENDS ON THE ELEVEN SOFT ONES LAID ALONG THE FOOT OF THE SHED. THIS IS THE 0063 REVIEW'S FINDING 4 AND THE DIRECTION OF REPAIR IS THE SAME: THE CHAPTER IS RIGHT AND THE RECORD WAS WRONG, SO THE RECORD IS CORRECTED AND THE PROSE WAS NOT TOUCHED FOR ANY OF THE FIVE.

second_measure_done_before_any_prose.the_second_reason_the_family_is_closed: The fault that caught 795 to 804 twice and nearly caught 815 to 824's own closings was eight of the ten standing on the same beat in different words. THE TEN CLOSINGS ABOVE STAND ON A MARK, AN EDGE, A STACK, A BAND, A TURN, A BEARER, A MEND, A STUB, A STACK AND THREE HOLES, AND THE TWO STACKS ARE TWENTY CHAPTERS APART IN THE BLOCK AND SIT ON OPPOSITE SIDES OF IT, ONE AT NUMBER TEN IN JULY AND ONE UNDER A KITCHEN WINDOW IN AUGUST.

the_second_measure_which_is_not_the_copy: WRITE THE TEN ENDINGS DOWN BEFORE THE FIRST CHAPTER, THEN READ THE TEN SENTENCES SIDE BY SIDE AND WRITE THREE WORDS ON WHAT EACH ONE IS ABOUT. IF TWO OF THE THREE-WORD DESCRIPTIONS MATCH, THAT ENDING IS WRONG HOWEVER DIFFERENT THE WORDS ARE. A TEN-TOKEN SPAN FINDS A COPY, AN ECHO IS A TIC, AND A TEMPLATE IS NEITHER. THE 0061 READ-BACK FOUND THE SAME BEAT IN EIGHT OF TEN AT A ZERO MEASURE AND 0063 FOUND FIVE ERRORS OF FACT THAT ITS ZERO MEASURE COULD NOT SEE, SO BOTH TOOLS ARE RUN HERE.
still_live_and_taken_up_by_nobody_here: Four pallets on bearers. A shutter that runs silently. A near gate square with a brace in it. A gate on a wall that shuts. A back door shut on its own frame. A cowl braced on a plate. A boundary run with scarfed bites. Grass on ground that has not had anything on it. A shelf under a window with a tub on it. A sack with a new bottom. Four feet of frost wall with its top course open. A spanner on a set of flags. Six feet of edging in a heap at the back of a house. Off the page and waiting on the man off the ring road, who has now sat out seven blocks: a figure for four rooms given aloud twice in a lock-up and written nowhere; a frame that is out of square and which its own man will find at the fitting; a landing wall with a bare patch on it and a mirror in a van; a fourth room at the top of a stair that nobody has priced or looked into. Three lines of paper shut in a drawer on purpose with the tools that would do them. A box in a corner of a lock-up whose lid is not nailed.

prohibitions_honoured.no_arithmetic_engine: Nothing is added up, nothing is priced, nothing is counted and no number is asked to agree with another. There is no figure-mismatch spread and no telephone.
prohibitions_honoured.water: No tap is run and no water is drawn, carried, poured or emptied by a person in any of the ten.
prohibitions_honoured.wet_jobs: NONE. No cement, no mortar and no new concrete anywhere in the ten. The two places the inheritance touches concrete remain 0784 and 0787, which are a human's. 0833 IS A DRY WALL COMING DOWN AND NO MORTAR GOES ANYWHERE NEAR IT.
prohibitions_honoured.standing_objects_untouched: The freeholder does not arrive. The line at ten is not put right. The ladder is not opened and no room is painted. The box behind the lock-up bench is not opened and nothing is asserted about its lid in either direction. The drawer with leads and screws is not opened. The drawer at ten stays shut. The front rooms at twelve and at nine are not entered and the kitchen at ten is not a front room and is not entered in any case. The report is not chased. The envelope is not turned. The bowl stays on its shelf and the ring on the tiles. No felt is nailed. No ply is nailed at number ten. THE STAPLE AT THE UNIT IS NOT DONE AND NO CARD MAY STAND ON IT, THE LATCH STAYS HOOKED BACK OVER THAT GATE FRAME, AND NO CARD MAY SAY APRIL OR A DATE. The four feet of frost wall and its open top course are not touched. The kitchen sash at twelve stays a hand's width low for good. The coal hole at nine stays shut with its load not looked into and the green furry middle not mentioned. The stone offcut across the hollow at nine is not lifted. The slab at nine stays tilting to the rail. The gate at nine stays open across the path on its two wedges and the odd job man's spanner is not picked up. THE TWO OVAL HOLES IN THE POST ABOVE THE GATE STRAP AT THE LOCK-UP ARE NOT FILLED AND NOT PLUGGED.
prohibitions_honoured.the_second_person: THE SECOND PERSON NEVER TOUCHES THE JOB, NEVER HOLDS ANYTHING, IS NEVER ASKED ABOUT IT, NEVER ASKS ABOUT IT AND NEVER LOOKS AT IT TWICE. NO CARD MAY HAVE A SECOND PAIR OF HANDS IN IT.
prohibitions_honoured.no_clock_and_no_tally: No closed clock time in any prose and no day tally in any prose.
prohibitions_honoured.everything_dry_and_from_the_ground: Every job is dry work and every job is done from the ground. No job goes on a roof, up a ladder, into a loft or into a manhole. A CARD THAT NEEDS THE WRITER TO GET UP ON SOMETHING IS A CARD THAT MUST BE REWRITTEN BEFORE IT IS USED, AND NO CARD IN THIS LIST AS WRITTEN NEEDS IT.

read_back.readers: The writer who took the block over from the saved work, reading all ten chapters whole with the band file in one hand and this file's four checks in the other, off the pages and not off any state file.
read_back.findings_returned: Twelve. Four of them are errors of fact no measure in this directory can see: 0830 carried a closed clock time in its last paragraph; 0830 called the bar she had stood on in 0795 'the first bar' inside a paragraph that opens on two bars leaning by the office door, so that the reader could not tell whether one of the two on the rack was the bar that was not the subject; 0832 said the bed the four posts stand in was a bed she had just taken the turf off, and the turf in 0829 came off the front bed while the privet is on the side wall; and 0834 ended on three holes where the body had already said the stool came out of one hole. Four more were the house form: 0825, 0826, 0827 and 0828 had their all-caps paragraph without its asterisks, which is four of ten and not a thing anybody would notice by reading, and 0830 and 0832 had three bold lines in the body, two of which state the card's stop in the card's own words. Two were the closing-image record standing against the page in five places and one figure of fact in it: the record said six feet of privet stub at 0832 and it is four feet. One was 0830 ending on the job, which its own rule forbids.
read_back.findings_fixed_in_the_prose: All twelve. The 0834 repair is the largest: the stool now comes up in three pieces, three rootstocks with a stub and a foot of cut root each, and the three holes are the three it came out of. The 0830 repair takes the ending off the rack and onto the third length by the far wall that she did not use, and takes the closed clock time out of the paragraph above it. No card changed its job, no band moved, no date moved, no family changed, and no standing object was touched.
